overall: Moves session lookup from the request handler into a new `SessionStore`, so handlers no longer talk to Redis directly. This makes the cache swappable and lets the store be tested without a server.

files.summary: Introduces `SessionStore` and its Redis implementation, and the interface handlers depend on.
The handler now takes a `SessionStore` instead of a Redis client.

hunks.summary: Replaces the direct `redis.Get` call with `store.Get`, so the handler no longer knows where sessions live.

diagrams.title: Handler to session storage
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  H[Handler] --> S[SessionStore]
  S --> R[(Redis)]
  classDef added fill:#d1fae5,stroke:#16a34a
  classDef changed fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#d97706
  class S added
  class H changed
diagrams.explanation: Before, the handler called Redis itself. Now it depends on `SessionStore` (green), and only that type knows about Redis, so the handler (amber) changed but its behavior did not.

diagrams.title: Loading a session
diagrams.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant H as Handler
  participant S as SessionStore
  participant R as Redis
  H->>S: Get(id)
  S->>R: GET session:id
  R-->>S: bytes
  S-->>H: Session
diagrams.explanation: The handler asks the store for a session; only the store talks to Redis and decodes the bytes.
